cleared.check: Lead L-582 for x86: the three x86 kernels of the evm2 jump destination scan at rev 35aa3280 (analyze_sse41, analyze_avx2, analyze_avx512vbmi in crates/evm2/src/bytecode/analysis/x86.rs, with analyze_scalar for the tail) were copied unchanged apart from visibility and the std feature switch, built with rustc 1.97.0 and run natively on a CPU with SSE4.1, AVX2 and AVX-512 VBMI
cleared.result: 442,577 bytecodes (the 24,009 byte Tempo PoolManager, 4,096 of its suffixes, PUSH1 to PUSH32 filled with 0x5b at 130 offsets and 11 tails, truncated pushes, 300,000 random codes biased to pushes and JUMPDEST, and uniform fills) give the same jump destination set as a specification reference in every kernel and in the CPU dispatch. Changing PUSHX by one makes about 360,000 cases fail in each SIMD kernel, so the harness sees a fault. A validator on x86 hardware runs one of these paths whatever its CPU.

cleared.check: Lead L-621: ruint 1.20.0 sub_x86_64 (_subborrow_u64 chain) against sub_fallback (borrowing_sub chain) in src/algorithms/mod.rs:149-191, which back algorithms::lt and cmp and therefore every U256 LT, GT and comparison in revm, including lt(mm, prod0) at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:25 and gt(remainder, prod0) at FullMath.sol:52
cleared.result: Both functions copied from the crate and run on 21,721,088 pairs of 256 bit operands (all 4-limb words of 12 edge limbs against edge partners and plus one neighbours, and 20 million random pairs sharing 0 to 4 top limbs): identical (difference OR, borrow) pairs and identical ordering against a schoolbook reference. ruint 1.20.0 has no other x86-only arithmetic path (only cmp.rs carries riscv branches). A non-x86 Arc validator would compute the same comparisons.

cleared.check: Release notes of revm-interpreter after 35.0.1 (Arc's pin) up to 43.0.2 for fixes on arithmetic, jumps, memory, copies and transient storage
cleared.result: The only interpreter fixes are a MemoryOOG return when memory.resize fails (43.0.0), a pop_address const-eval change, a CREATE depth check for EIP-8037 and the memory_limit placement. In 35.0.1 SharedMemory::resize always returns true and gas for the new size is charged first, so an Arc validator cannot continue on a failed resize; the PoolManager uses no CREATE.

leadResults.answer: The T15 release is not yet published (node operator page, 2026-11-25) and main still pins evm2 35aa3280 and ruint 1.21.1, so there is no new lock to diff. The battery, the targeted set including the 8,908 vectors of the ruint 1.21.0 fault, and both script sets were run under T14 rules through a simulated block time and match. Carried forward as a new lead to run with the T15 timestamp once the release exists.

As published on 2026-11-25 the T15 page covers only TIP-1166 (configurable account voucher signers), gives no timestamps and says other features will be added when specified; the node operator page lists TIP-1166 as the only T15 TIP. TIP-1094 is not in the published T15 scope, so F-135 does not apply on mainnet on the published plan. This can change when the release is published (new lead).

rpc.mainnet.arc.io answers v0.8.6-rc1 (37812c61) and arc.drpc.org v0.8.6 (8e8edb7a); arc-rpc.publicnode.com now serves a Cloudflare challenge and could not be queried. No tag after v0.8.6 exists (v0.8.7, v0.8.8, v0.9.0 return 404). v0.8.5 and v0.8.6 have identical opcode.rs and evm.rs and pin the same revm 38.0.0, revm-interpreter 35.0.1 and ruint 1.20.0.

For x86: the evm2 scan at 35aa3280 has three x86 kernels chosen at run time (AVX-512 VBMI, then AVX2, then SSE4.1) plus a scalar tail, and NEON on aarch64. The x86 kernels were copied unchanged and run natively on 442,577 bytecodes including the PoolManager and PUSH data with 0x5b in every lane; all agree with a specification reference, and a planted fault is caught. The release binary has no compiler stage (OPCODES.md). The NEON kernel was not run here (new lead).

evm2 at 35aa3280 allows a nested transaction (enter_execution records was_running) and documents set_initial_call_depth as forbidden from a precompile. crates/zones/* are zone chain crates and crates/consensus is the consensus layer; neither executes inside a Tempo L1 user call by design, but their files were not read line by line this cycle because no code search is available. The suite under T14 time shows no state carried between calls.

The mainnet build is tempo/v1.19.1 on evm2 35aa3280 without the optional compiler (OPCODES.md, cycles 13 and 15); transient storage is cleared in clear_transaction_state per transaction (cycle 2); the v1.18.4 fix adds a gas check before a precompile or the T14 account marker copies its input (cycle 7). The battery and both script sets pass at the current time and under T14 rules.

Mainnet has not adopted a release after v1.19.1, and v1.19.1 and main both pin evm2 35aa3280, the revision cycle 13 read file by file. Nothing new to read until a new tag appears; L-804's successor covers that.

Zero7 and Zero8 are active on mainnet since 1789052400 (2026-09-10) and require v0.8.0 or later; v0.8.0 lists the ruint correction for overflow flags and shift amounts, and every v0.8.x tag pins ruint 1.20.0 and revm-interpreter 35.0.1. Which exact release each validator runs is not published, but every release that can follow the chain has the same arithmetic.

sub_x86_64 and sub_fallback of ruint 1.20.0 agree on 21.7 million 256 bit operand pairs with each other and with a reference, so LT, GT and the comparisons of FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:25, 52) give the same result on x86 and non-x86 builds. Whether any Arc validator runs on non-x86 hardware is still not published.
